Good web design Detroit shoppers respond to starts with a street address. Across the city, owners are signing leases on long-empty storefronts, opening bakeries, barbershops, boutiques and cafes on corridors that have seen hard years, and counting on neighbors to walk in. Before most of those neighbors walk in, they look the place up. This page is for that owner: the person with a build-out underway and a grand opening on the calendar. Dominion Web Design Pro writes the site by hand, shows you a free demo first, and charges once.

A grant opens the doors. A website tells people they are open.

Detroit has put real money into new storefronts. Motor City Match, run with the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation, gives grants to entrepreneurs opening brick-and-mortar businesses in the city and to existing businesses improving their spaces, along with business services, classes and help matching owners with buildings. In its 25th round the program awarded about $1.24 million to 23 new businesses spread across 19 neighborhoods, and the city says more than $17.1 million has gone out since federal relief money doubled the program's grant funding in August 2022.

Money for a build-out does not bring customers by itself. A shop that opened last month has no reviews, no history in search results and no word of mouth yet. The website is often the first thing a curious neighbor finds, and it has to answer the basics fast: what you sell, when you are open, and exactly which block you are on.

Four Detroit corridors, four different first impressions

Detroit is a big city of about 645,700 people, by the Census Bureau's July 2024 estimate, and its commercial streets do not share one customer. A site that works on one corridor can miss on another. Here is how the lead message changes from place to place.

CorridorWhat is thereWhat your home page should lead with
Avenue of Fashion, Livernois between Seven and Eight MileA shopping strip that took its name in the late 1950s for clothing and specialty shops, known for Black-owned businesses, now mixing boutiques with restaurants, bars and professional services after a rebuilt streetscape with wider sidewalks.Who owns it and what makes the shop distinct, plus parking and the nearest cross street.
Eastern MarketA public market at its present site since 1891, the oldest continuously operating public market in Michigan, with more than 150 businesses selling produce, meat, flowers and specialty foods, and big Saturday crowds.Which days you sell, which shed or storefront you are in, and what is fresh this week.
Corktown, along Michigan AvenueDetroit's oldest surviving neighborhood, named for Irish settlers from County Cork, with a commercial strip of bars, restaurants, coffee and shops that has grown over the past decade.Hours, reservations or wait times, and what someone visiting from downtown should order first.
Southwest Detroit, Bagley and West VernorThe heart of Mexicantown, where the Bagley and West Vernor commercial area holds bakeries, taquerias, grocers and tortilla makers on both sides of I-75.The menu or product list, hours, and directions that make sense to someone crossing from the freeway.

None of this needs a big site. It needs the right few facts on the first screen of a phone, written in your own words rather than a template's.

Web design Detroit openings need: a timeline that starts before the sign goes up

The best time to build a storefront site is during the build-out, not after the ribbon cutting. Here is how the work lines up with a typical opening.

  1. While the contractors are insideSend your business name, your address and a few lines about what you will sell. Maurice builds a free demo you can open on your phone and show your partners or your landlord.
  2. Six weeks or so before openingApprove the pages, add your real hours and a "coming soon" note, and start collecting interest through the contact form. Starter goes live in 7 to 14 days, which leaves room for changes.
  3. Opening weekSwap the coming soon note for opening hours, post photos of the finished space, and make sure the address on the site matches your Google Business Profile exactly.
  4. The first monthsAdd the menu changes, new products, events and photos of regulars' favorite items. A site that changes tells people and search engines the shop is alive.

Detroit web design company, agency or one person?

Search for a Detroit web design company and you will find large agencies, freelancers and national template builders, all priced differently and often not priced at all until after a sales call. For a first storefront, the deciding questions are simple: what will it cost in dollars, who owns the site when it is done, and can you see something real before you pay?

Our answers are printed. Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages with a contact form, Google Maps, your hours and links to Facebook and Instagram. Pro is $997 for ten pages, a photo gallery, local SEO setup with schema and Google Business Profile setup, your Google reviews shown on the site and ten city pages; its AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. Agency is $1,997 with keyword research first and a page for every town and service worth targeting, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks; it includes AI phone agent setup, and the agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time. Every price is one time, and you own the site outright.

Detroit web design agencies are the better fit if you want a team in a room with you every month, or a custom ordering system. If you want affordable web design Detroit customers can actually use, built by the person you talk to, that is what we do.

Not every Detroit business has a storefront

The comeback is not only shops. Landscapers, cleaners, roofers, auto techs and home repair crews work out of trucks and garages and travel neighborhood to neighborhood, from the east side to Southwest and up into the suburbs. A homeowner looking for them does not type a corridor name. They type the job and the place they live.

For those businesses the site should be organized around services and service areas: a page for each kind of work, photos of real jobs, and a clear list of the neighborhoods and towns you drive to. Pro's ten city pages exist for exactly this, each one researched and written for that place instead of a list of names pasted at the bottom of a page.

Why the neighborhood name belongs on the page

Google says local results depend mostly on three things: relevance, meaning how well a listing matches what someone searched; distance from the searcher or the place named in the search; and prominence, meaning how well known the business is. A new storefront starts with little prominence. Relevance is the part you control on day one, and it rests on plain words: the service, the neighborhood, the corridor, the cross street.

That is why we put "Livernois" or "Bagley" or "Eastern Market" where it belongs instead of a vague "serving Metro Detroit." Nobody can promise a ranking, and we will not. What we can do is make sure the site says clearly what you do and where you do it.

Detroit help to line up before you sign a lease

  • Detroit Economic Growth CorporationRuns Motor City Match with the city: grants for new and existing brick-and-mortar businesses, plus business services and workshops.
  • TechTown DetroitWayne State's entrepreneurship hub runs Retail Boot Camp, an intensive 12-week program for people opening brick-and-mortar shops in Wayne County, plus one-on-one coaching.
  • Michigan SBDC, Southeast Michigan RegionNo-cost consulting, market research and business education for Wayne, Oakland and Macomb counties, based at Eastern Michigan University.
  • Detroit Regional ChamberThe regional chamber of commerce, known statewide for its yearly Mackinac Policy Conference, with membership open to small businesses.

Michigan runs on small firms. The SBA Office of Advocacy's 2024 profile counted 945,788 small businesses in the state, 99.6% of all Michigan businesses, employing 47.4% of the state's workers. Detroit is also a majority Black city, about three in four residents by Census figures, and Dominion Web Design Pro is a Black-owned business, owned and run by Maurice Johnson.

Common questions

Is there affordable web design in Detroit without a monthly contract?

Yes. Dominion Web Design Pro charges once: $497 for Starter, $997 for Pro or $1,997 for Agency. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep the AI agent, or $49 a month without it, and there is no long contract to sign. Affordable should still mean the pages are written for your shop and your block, so you see a free demo before you pay anything.

What should a Detroit web design company include for a new storefront?

At minimum: your address and the corridor or neighborhood you are on, hours, a map, parking or transit notes, a phone number that dials with one tap, and a contact form that emails you. Add photos of the inside of the shop and a short story of who runs it. Starter covers all of that in five pages and goes live in 7 to 14 days, so a site can be up before a grand opening if you start early.

How do I compare Detroit web design agencies with a single builder?

Put the same four questions to each: the full price in dollars, who owns the site and the domain, what changes cost after launch, and whether you can see work built for your business before paying. An agency brings a team and usually a bigger budget. A single builder means you talk to the person doing the work. We are the second kind, working remotely, and our prices are printed on the site.

What is the difference between web design and web development?

Web design is what a customer sees and reads: the words, layout, photos and buttons. Web development is the engineering underneath, and on large projects it means custom software such as portals, online ordering systems or apps. A storefront usually needs design done well on a fast, clean build. Our sites include that build, but we do not make custom software or online stores, and we will tell you if your project needs a different kind of firm.

Can you build pages for the suburbs as well as the city?

Yes, for any town you really serve. Pro includes ten city pages, each researched and written for that place, which suits a contractor or mobile service working the city and nearby suburbs. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole area and builds a page for each town and service pair worth having, usually 30 to 60 pages.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
